title: Psalms Chapter 46 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 46 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 46 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 46.

questions.question: According to Psalms 46:1, God is our refuge and strength, and what else?
options: A very present help in trouble
A mighty fortress
A guiding light
A loving father
questions.correctAnswer: A very present help in trouble
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:1 states that God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 46:2 says we will fear even if the earth is removed.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:2 says 'Therefore will not we fear, though the earth be removed,' meaning we will not fear even if the earth is removed.

questions.question: What natural event is mentioned in Psalms 46:3 as causing the mountains to shake?
options: The swelling of troubled waters
A great earthquake
A strong wind
A volcanic eruption
questions.correctAnswer: The swelling of troubled waters
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:3 states 'Though the waters thereof roar and be troubled, though the mountains shake with the swelling thereof.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 46:4, what makes glad the city of God?
options: A river and its streams
The sun and moon
The mountains and hills
The birds and animals
questions.correctAnswer: A river and its streams
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:4 says, 'There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 46:5 says God is in the midst of the city and it shall not be moved.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:5 states 'God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved.'

questions.question: Who is the chief musician mentioned in Psalms 46:1 for whom this song is written?
options: Sons of Korah
David
Asaph
Heman
questions.correctAnswer: Sons of Korah
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:1 says 'To the chief Musician for the sons of Korah, A Song upon Alamoth.'

questions.question: In Psalms 46:2, what is said about the mountains?
options: They may be carried into the midst of the sea
They will never move
They will be covered with snow
They will grow taller
questions.correctAnswer: They may be carried into the midst of the sea
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:2 states 'though the mountains be carried into the midst of the sea.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 46:3 describes the waters as calm and peaceful.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:3 says 'Though the waters thereof roar and be troubled,' so the waters are not calm.

questions.question: What is described as the 'holy place of the tabernacles of the most High' in Psalms 46:4?
options: The city of God
Mount Sinai
Jerusalem
The temple
questions.correctAnswer: The city of God
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:4 refers to 'the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the most High.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 46:1, what is God to us?
options: Refuge and strength
Light and salvation
Peace and comfort
Judge and king
questions.correctAnswer: Refuge and strength
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:1 states 'God is our refuge and strength.'

questions.question: In Psalms 46:3, what does the verse say the mountains do?
options: Shake with the swelling of troubled waters
Stand firm and unmoved
Are covered with snow
Are carved by the rivers
questions.correctAnswer: Shake with the swelling of troubled waters
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:3 mentions 'though the mountains shake with the swelling thereof.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 46:2 encourages us not to fear even if the earth is removed.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:2 states 'Therefore will not we fear, though the earth be removed,' encouraging us not to fear.

questions.question: Which phrase comes first in Psalms 46:1?
options: God is our refuge and strength
A Song upon Alamoth
To the chief Musician for the sons of Korah
A very present help in trouble
questions.correctAnswer: To the chief Musician for the sons of Korah
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:1 begins with 'To the chief Musician for the sons of Korah' before mentioning the other phrases.

questions.question: What will the streams of the river do according to Psalms 46:4?
options: Make glad the city of God
Dry up and disappear
Flood the surrounding lands
Make the mountains grow
questions.correctAnswer: Make glad the city of God
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:4 says 'the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 46:5, when will God help the city?
options: Right early
At noon
At night
In the evening
questions.correctAnswer: Right early
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:5 says 'God shall help her, and that right early.'

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 46 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 46 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 46:5, what assurance is given about the city where God dwells?
options: She shall not be moved and God will help her early
She will face many troubles and be shaken
She will be abandoned in times of trouble
She will be destroyed by the kingdoms
questions.correctAnswer: She shall not be moved and God will help her early
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:5 states that God is in the midst of the city, so she shall not be moved and God will help her early, assuring stability and divine assistance.

questions.question: What imagery is used in Psalms 46:6 to describe God's power over nations and the earth?
options: He uttered his voice and the earth melted
He sent fire to consume the heathen
He built mountains to protect the kingdoms
He commanded the waters to rise up
questions.correctAnswer: He uttered his voice and the earth melted
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:6 uses powerful imagery of God uttering His voice causing the earth to melt, showing His sovereign power over raging nations and kingdoms.

questions.question: What repeated declaration in Psalms 46:7 and 46:11 emphasizes God’s protective presence?
options: The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge
God will punish the wicked swiftly
The mountains will be carried into the sea
The rivers shall dry up
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge
questions.explanation: Both Psalms 46:7 and 46:11 affirm that the LORD of hosts is with us and is our refuge, highlighting God's continual protection and presence.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 46:8, what is the purpose of beholding the works of the LORD?
options: To see the desolations He has made on the earth
To witness the prosperity of the nations
To admire the beauty of creation
To learn how to build cities
questions.correctAnswer: To see the desolations He has made on the earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:8 invites us to observe the works of the LORD, specifically the desolations He has made, emphasizing God's sovereignty over all earthly events.

questions.question: How does Psalms 46:5-6 together teach us about God’s response to chaos and threats?
options: God is present in His city to keep it stable, and He can cause the earth to melt by His voice when kingdoms rage
God ignores the chaos and allows the earth to be moved freely
God abandons His city but punishes the nations severely
The city will be shaken but God will protect the mountains
questions.correctAnswer: God is present in His city to keep it stable, and He can cause the earth to melt by His voice when kingdoms rage
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 together show God’s protective presence stabilizing His city while exercising supreme power over nations and natural elements during chaos.

questions.question: What biblical virtue is exemplified by the repeated phrase in Psalms 46:7 and 46:11, 'The God of Jacob is our refuge'?
options: Faith and trust in God’s protection
Pride in human strength
Fear of earthly kingdoms
Self-reliance in times of trouble
questions.correctAnswer: Faith and trust in God’s protection
questions.explanation: The repeated assurance that God is our refuge encourages believers to place their faith and trust in God's protection rather than worldly powers.

questions.question: A believer feels overwhelmed by global conflicts and natural disasters. Based on Psalms 46:5-8, what truth should encourage them?
options: God dwells in His city and remains unshaken; He controls the earth and nations even amidst chaos
The earth is abandoned by God and is subject to random destruction
Only human efforts can bring peace and stability
God will let the earth be destroyed without intervention
questions.correctAnswer: God dwells in His city and remains unshaken; He controls the earth and nations even amidst chaos
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:5-8 teaches that God’s presence ensures stability and that He has sovereign control over nations and natural events, offering hope amid turmoil.

questions.question: According to Psalms 46:8-9, what actions does God take to bring peace to the earth?
options: He makes wars to cease, breaks the bow and spear, and burns the chariot
He encourages kingdoms to fight for dominance
He causes floods to punish the earth
He removes rivers to stop trade
questions.correctAnswer: He makes wars to cease, breaks the bow and spear, and burns the chariot
questions.explanation: Verses 8-9 describe God’s active role in ending wars and destroying instruments of war, symbolizing His desire for peace on earth.

questions.question: What does Psalms 46:10 instruct believers to do, and what is promised will follow?
options: Be still and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the heathen and in the earth
Fight bravely against enemies; victory will come by strength
Build strong cities; safety will be guaranteed
Pray loudly for deliverance; troubles will end immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Be still and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the heathen and in the earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:10 calls for calm trust in God’s sovereignty, promising His exaltation among nations as a result of this faith.

questions.question: What does Psalms 46:5 suggest about the timing of God's help?
options: God shall help her, and that right early
God will delay help until later
Help will come only after much suffering
Help depends on human effort
questions.correctAnswer: God shall help her, and that right early
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that God will provide help promptly, giving assurance of timely divine intervention.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 46:6, the kingdoms remain unmoved despite the rage of the heathen.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:6 states that the heathen raged and the kingdoms were moved, indicating instability among the kingdoms.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 46:7 asserts that God is a refuge for the people of Jacob.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:7 declares that the LORD of hosts is with us and that the God of Jacob is our refuge, affirming God’s protective role.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 46:8 invites believers to ignore the works of the LORD, especially the desolations He has made.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Contrary to ignoring, Psalms 46:8 calls believers to come and behold the works of the LORD, including the desolations He has made, emphasizing awareness of God's sovereign acts.

questions.question: What does Psalms 46:9 teach about God's control over instruments of war?
options: God breaks the bow, cuts the spear, and burns the chariot to bring peace
God empowers weapons for victory
God ignores the instruments of war
God hides the weapons in secret places
questions.correctAnswer: God breaks the bow, cuts the spear, and burns the chariot to bring peace
questions.explanation: Verse 9 explains that God actively disables the weapons of war to cause wars to cease, illustrating His desire for peace.

questions.question: How does Psalms 46:10-11 together encourage believers during times of conflict?
options: Be still and acknowledge God's sovereignty, for He is exalted and is our refuge
Fight aggressively to defend your land
Seek alliances with powerful kingdoms
Ignore troubles and live for personal gain
questions.correctAnswer: Be still and acknowledge God's sovereignty, for He is exalted and is our refuge
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 encourage calm trust in God’s power and presence, assuring believers that God is exalted and is their refuge amid conflict.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 46 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 46.

questions.question: According to Psalms 46:9, what does God do to make wars cease unto the end of the earth?
options: He breaks the bow, cuts the spear in sunder, and burns the chariot in the fire
He sends plagues upon the enemies
He causes earthquakes to destroy armies
He commands angels to fight for His people
questions.correctAnswer: He breaks the bow, cuts the spear in sunder, and burns the chariot in the fire
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:9 explicitly states that God makes wars cease by breaking the bow, cutting the spear in sunder, and burning the chariot in the fire, symbolizing the end of earthly instruments of war.

questions.question: In Psalms 46:10, what is the central command given to the listener?
options: Be still, and know that I am God
Go forth and conquer in My name
Sing praises to the Lord
Build a sanctuary for Me
questions.correctAnswer: Be still, and know that I am God
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:10 commands the listener to 'Be still, and know that I am God,' emphasizing trust and recognition of God's sovereignty amid chaos.

questions.question: Which phrase in Psalms 46:11 echoes a refrain found earlier in the chapter, emphasizing God's presence?
options: "The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge"
"The earth melted when He uttered His voice"
"Though the mountains be carried into the midst of the sea"
"There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God"
questions.correctAnswer: "The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge"
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:11 repeats the phrase from Psalms 46:7, forming an inclusio that brackets the psalm and stresses God’s protective presence.

questions.question: What literary device is demonstrated by the repetition of 'The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge' in Psalms 46:7 and 46:11?
options: Inclusio
Chiasm
Parallelism
Metaphor
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The repetition of this phrase at both the beginning and end of the psalm creates an inclusio, framing the psalm with a thematic emphasis on God’s protective presence (Psalms 46:7 and Psalms 46:11).

questions.question: Which Old Testament prophecy is echoed in Psalms 46:10’s declaration, 'I will be exalted among the heathen'?
options: Isaiah 2:11 - The Lord will be exalted in that day
Genesis 1:1 - In the beginning God created
Exodus 20:3 - Thou shalt have no other gods before me
Daniel 7:14 - Dominion given to the Son of Man
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 2:11 - The Lord will be exalted in that day
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:10’s theme of God’s exaltation among the nations echoes Isaiah 2:11, which speaks of the Lord being exalted in the day of judgment, highlighting divine sovereignty over all peoples.

questions.question: The phrase 'He breaketh the bow, and cutteth the spear in sunder' in Psalms 46:9 is an example of what type of parallelism?
options: Synonymous parallelism
Antithetic parallelism
Synthetic parallelism
Chiastic parallelism
questions.correctAnswer: Synonymous parallelism
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:9 uses synonymous parallelism by repeating similar ideas about destruction of weapons to emphasize God's power to stop war.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 46:10 commands believers to be silent and recognize God's sovereignty.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:10 says, 'Be still, and know that I am God,' which commands believers to be silent and acknowledge God's sovereignty.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Alamoth,' mentioned in the Psalm 46 title, most likely refer to?
options: A musical term indicating a high-pitched instrument or female voices
A type of ancient weapon
The name of a city in Israel
A festival celebrated by the sons of Korah
questions.correctAnswer: A musical term indicating a high-pitched instrument or female voices
questions.explanation: The term 'Alamoth' in Psalms 46:1’s title is understood to be a musical direction, referring to high-pitched sounds or female voices, reflecting the psalm's liturgical use.

questions.question: According to Psalms 46:9-10, what ultimate effect does God’s power have on earthly conflicts?
options: Wars cease and God is exalted among the nations
Armies grow stronger and win battles
Kings gain more territory
The earth is destroyed by war
questions.correctAnswer: Wars cease and God is exalted among the nations
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:9-10 shows that God causes wars to cease and will be exalted among the nations, highlighting His ultimate authority over earthly conflicts.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse reflects the theme of God's exaltation among the nations as proclaimed in Psalms 46:10?
options: Philippians 2:9 - God hath highly exalted him
John 3:16 - For God so loved the world
Romans 8:28 - All things work together for good
Hebrews 11:1 - Faith is the substance of things hoped for
questions.correctAnswer: Philippians 2:9 - God hath highly exalted him
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:9 echoes the theme of exaltation in Psalms 46:10, describing God's exaltation of Christ above all names, connecting Old Testament sovereignty to New Testament fulfillment.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 46 portrays God as an unreliable refuge in times of trouble.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:1 and 46:11 clearly describe God as a 'refuge and strength' and a 'very present help in trouble,' portraying Him as a reliable protector.

questions.question: How does Psalms 46:9 use imagery to describe the end of war?
options: By depicting the breaking and burning of weapons and chariots
By describing a peaceful negotiation between nations
By portraying the flight of soldiers from battle
By highlighting the silence of the battlefield
questions.correctAnswer: By depicting the breaking and burning of weapons and chariots
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:9 uses vivid imagery of breaking bows, cutting spears, and burning chariots to symbolize the destruction of war tools and the cessation of conflict.

questions.question: Which phrase in Psalms 46 emphasizes God's protection of the city of God, and what does this symbolize?
options: "God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved" - symbolizing divine security for Jerusalem
"Though the waters roar and be troubled" - symbolizing chaos around the city
"The mountains shake with the swelling thereof" - symbolizing natural disasters
"The heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved" - symbolizing political turmoil
questions.correctAnswer: "God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved" - symbolizing divine security for Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:5 states, 'God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved,' symbolizing God's protective presence securing the city of Jerusalem.

questions.question: What historical or cultural context helps explain the imagery of bows, spears, and chariots in Psalms 46:9?
options: These were common ancient Near Eastern weapons symbolizing military power
They refer to symbolic spiritual battles in heaven
They were ceremonial items used in Israelite worship
They represent agricultural tools used in ancient Israel
questions.correctAnswer: These were common ancient Near Eastern weapons symbolizing military power
questions.explanation: In the ancient Near East, bows, spears, and chariots were standard military equipment, so their destruction in Psalms 46:9 symbolizes the end of physical warfare.

questions.question: Which theme from Psalms 46 is also a major theme in Isaiah 40, particularly in the call to 'Be still, and know that I am God'?
options: God’s sovereignty and the call to trust Him amidst turmoil
The promise of a new temple
The coming of a Messiah to judge the nations
The establishment of an everlasting kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereignty and the call to trust Him amidst turmoil
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40 emphasizes God's sovereign power and encourages the people to trust Him, paralleling Psalms 46:10’s call to 'Be still, and know that I am God.'

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 46 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 46 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What primary attribute of God is emphasized in Psalms 46:1 when He is called 'our refuge and strength'?
options: God is omniscient
God is a present help in trouble
God is distant and passive
God is primarily a judge
questions.correctAnswer: God is a present help in trouble
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:1 states that God is 'a very present help in trouble,' emphasizing His active, immediate assistance and protection, which highlights His attribute of being a refuge and strength.

questions.question: According to Psalms 46:2, how should believers respond when the earth is removed and mountains are carried into the sea?
options: They should fear greatly
They should remain fearless
They should flee to the mountains
They should seek new earthly kingdoms
questions.correctAnswer: They should remain fearless
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:2 declares 'Therefore will not we fear, though the earth be removed,' teaching the doctrine of trust in God’s sovereignty over creation, which assures believers that faith transcends even cosmic upheaval.

questions.question: What does the imagery of roaring and troubled waters in Psalms 46:3 primarily signify about God’s control over chaos?
options: God is indifferent to natural disasters
God causes chaos to punish the wicked
God sovereignly controls chaotic and destructive forces
God only controls peaceful times
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly controls chaotic and destructive forces
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:3 describes waters roaring and mountains shaking, symbolizing chaos and judgment, but this is under God’s sovereign control, illustrating His dominion over natural and cosmic disorder.

questions.question: In Psalms 46:4, what theological significance does the river that makes glad the city of God have?
options: It symbolizes God’s judgment upon enemies
It represents the sustaining and joyful presence of God
It depicts a literal river for irrigation
It foretells a future drought
questions.correctAnswer: It represents the sustaining and joyful presence of God
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:4’s river that gladdens the city of God symbolizes divine provision and joy flowing into the dwelling place of God’s people, reflecting God’s sustaining presence and blessing.

questions.question: What doctrine is highlighted by the statement in Psalms 46:5 that 'God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved'?
options: The immutability of God’s covenant protection
The doctrine of predestination
The doctrine of eternal punishment
The necessity of works for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: The immutability of God’s covenant protection
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:5 teaches that with God present, the city (representing God's covenant people) is immovable and secure, illustrating the unchanging, reliable nature of God's protective covenant.

questions.question: What does Psalms 46:6 reveal about God's power in relation to earthly kingdoms and nations?
options: God passively observes kingdoms
God actively judges and causes upheaval among nations
God supports all kingdoms equally
God is limited to spiritual realms only
questions.correctAnswer: God actively judges and causes upheaval among nations
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:6 shows that when the heathen rage and kingdoms move, God’s voice causes the earth to melt, highlighting His sovereign power to intervene and judge earthly powers.

questions.question: How does Psalms 46:7 contribute to the doctrine of God's protective presence for His covenant people?
options: God occasionally helps Israel
The LORD of hosts is with us and is our refuge continually
God favors only the priests
God’s presence is unpredictable
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD of hosts is with us and is our refuge continually
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:7 affirms the ongoing presence of the LORD of hosts with His people, underscoring the doctrine that God is their continuous refuge and protector.

questions.question: What does Psalms 46:8 invite believers to do concerning the works of the LORD?
options: Ignore His works
Be fearful of His wrath only
Behold and consider the desolations He has made
Celebrate human achievements instead
questions.correctAnswer: Behold and consider the desolations He has made
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:8 calls believers to attentively observe God’s mighty works, especially His judgment manifested as desolations on earth, which teaches reverence and acknowledgment of God’s power.

questions.question: Which doctrine is most clearly illustrated in Psalms 46:9 where God 'maketh wars to cease' and 'breaketh the bow'?
options: Doctrine of pacifism
Doctrine of God's sovereign peace and judgment over war
Doctrine of eternal conflict
Doctrine of human self-defense
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of God's sovereign peace and judgment over war
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:9 teaches that God alone controls the cessation of wars and the destruction of weapons, affirming His sovereign authority over peace and judgment in human conflict.

questions.question: What theological truth does Psalms 46:10 convey with 'Be still, and know that I am God'?
options: God is unknowable
God desires trust and recognition of His sovereignty
God demands silence from His people
God is only known through works
questions.correctAnswer: God desires trust and recognition of His sovereignty
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:10 calls for stillness and acknowledgment of God's identity, emphasizing the doctrine that faith involves trusting God’s sovereignty amidst turmoil.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching about God’s protection and presence is conveyed by Psalms 46:5 and Psalms 46:11?
options: God’s presence is temporary and unreliable
God dwells with His people, making them immovable and their refuge
God is absent during troubles
God only protects the physical city
questions.correctAnswer: God dwells with His people, making them immovable and their refuge
questions.explanation: Both Psalms 46:5 and 46:11 emphasize that God’s presence within His people ensures their stability and safety, teaching His abiding and protective presence as their refuge.

questions.question: How do Psalms 46:6 and Psalms 46:9 together reveal God’s authority over earthly powers and warfare?
options: God allows kingdoms to rule independently
God passively watches wars
God actively intervenes causing kingdoms to shake and wars to cease
God supports only one nation
questions.correctAnswer: God actively intervenes causing kingdoms to shake and wars to cease
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:6 depicts God's voice melting the earth amidst raging nations, and Psalms 46:9 shows God making wars cease, illustrating His sovereign control over political and military realms.

questions.question: What theological significance does the mention of 'the city of God' and 'the tabernacles of the most High' in Psalms 46:4 have in biblical redemptive history?
options: It refers only to a physical city without spiritual meaning
It symbolizes God's dwelling among His redeemed people, foreshadowing the New Testament temple of the Spirit
It predicts the destruction of Jerusalem only
It denies God's presence with His people
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes God's dwelling among His redeemed people, foreshadowing the New Testament temple of the Spirit
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:4’s reference to 'the city of God' and 'tabernacles' points to God's presence with His people, which in redemptive history anticipates the indwelling of God by the Holy Spirit in believers (cf. John 14:23; 1 Corinthians 3:16).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Psalms 46 teaches a passive God who does not intervene in human affairs. What does Psalms 46:6-7 actually teach about God's involvement with His people and the earth?
options: God remains distant and uninvolved
God passively observes but does not act
God actively intervenes by shaking kingdoms and is present with His people as their refuge
God endorses all human actions without judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God actively intervenes by shaking kingdoms and is present with His people as their refuge
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:6-7 shows God uttering His voice causing the earth to melt and affirming that the LORD of hosts is with His people, demonstrating His active intervention and protective presence, countering sceptical claims.

questions.question: What combined teaching about divine peace and exaltation is found in Psalms 46:9-10?
options: God allows endless war and remains hidden
God ceases wars and declares His exaltation among all nations
God exalts only Israel and promotes conflict
God's peace is limited to earthly kings
questions.correctAnswer: God ceases wars and declares His exaltation among all nations
questions.explanation: Psalms 46:9 teaches that God makes wars cease, and 46:10 declares God's exaltation among the heathen and earth, teaching that divine peace accompanies God's universal reign and glory.
